prompt.v: A wheel of radius 10 centimeters turns at 130 revolutions per minute. How fast does a point on its rim move, in meters per second, to 1 decimal place?

problems.text: linear speed: r 10 cm, rpm 130, want m per s to 1 dp
problems.explain: ω = 130 × 2π = 260π radians per minute, so v = rω = 10 × 260π cm per minute. Per second, ÷ 60; in meters, ÷ 100: 2600π ÷ 60 ÷ 100 ≈ 1.3614, which is 1.4 to 1 decimal place. (Leaving out the 2π counts turns, not distance.) So 1.4 meters per second.

problems.explain: ω = 350 × 2π = 700π radians per minute, so v = rω = 10 × 700π cm per minute. Per second, ÷ 60; in meters, ÷ 100: 7000π ÷ 60 ÷ 100 ≈ 3.6652, which is 3.7 to 1 decimal place. (Leaving out the 2π counts turns, not distance.) So 3.7 meters per second.

problems.explain: ω = 400 × 2π = 800π radians per minute, so v = rω = 12 × 800π cm per minute. Per second, ÷ 60; in meters, ÷ 100: 9600π ÷ 60 ÷ 100 ≈ 5.0265, which is 5.0 to 1 decimal place. (Leaving out the 2π counts turns, not distance.) So 5.0 meters per second.

problems.explain: ω = 190 × 2π = 380π radians per minute, so v = rω = 14 × 380π in per minute. Per second, ÷ 60; in feet, ÷ 12: 5320π ÷ 60 ÷ 12 ≈ 23.2129, which is 23.2 to 1 decimal place. (Leaving out the 2π counts turns, not distance.) So 23.2 feet per second.

problems.explain: ω = 70 × 2π = 140π radians per minute, so v = rω = 16 × 140π in per minute. Per second, ÷ 60; in feet, ÷ 12: 2240π ÷ 60 ÷ 12 ≈ 9.7738, which is 9.8 to 1 decimal place. (Leaving out the 2π counts turns, not distance.) So 9.8 feet per second.

problems.explain: ω = 220 × 2π = 440π radians per minute, so v = rω = 19 × 440π in per minute. Per second, ÷ 60; in feet, ÷ 12: 8360π ÷ 60 ÷ 12 ≈ 36.4774, which is 36.5 to 1 decimal place. (Leaving out the 2π counts turns, not distance.) So 36.5 feet per second.

problems.explain: ω = 390 × 2π = 780π radians per minute, so v = rω = 21 × 780π in per minute. Per second, ÷ 60; in feet, ÷ 12: 16380π ÷ 60 ÷ 12 ≈ 71.4712, which is 71.5 to 1 decimal place. (Leaving out the 2π counts turns, not distance.) So 71.5 feet per second.

problems.explain: ω = 270 × 2π = 540π radians per minute, so v = rω = 23 × 540π in per minute. Per second, ÷ 60; in feet, ÷ 12: 12420π ÷ 60 ÷ 12 ≈ 54.1925, which is 54.2 to 1 decimal place. (Leaving out the 2π counts turns, not distance.) So 54.2 feet per second.

problems.explain: ω = 50 × 2π = 100π radians per minute, so v = rω = 25 × 100π in per minute. Per second, ÷ 60; in feet, ÷ 12: 2500π ÷ 60 ÷ 12 ≈ 10.9083, which is 10.9 to 1 decimal place. (Leaving out the 2π counts turns, not distance.) So 10.9 feet per second.

problems.explain: ω = 90 × 2π = 180π radians per minute, so v = rω = 30 × 180π in per minute. Per second, ÷ 60; in feet, ÷ 12: 5400π ÷ 60 ÷ 12 ≈ 23.5619, which is 23.6 to 1 decimal place. (Leaving out the 2π counts turns, not distance.) So 23.6 feet per second.

problems.explain: ω = 380 × 2π = 760π radians per minute, so v = rω = 5 × 760π in per minute. Per second, ÷ 60; in feet, ÷ 12: 3800π ÷ 60 ÷ 12 ≈ 16.5806, which is 16.6 to 1 decimal place. (Leaving out the 2π counts turns, not distance.) So 16.6 feet per second.

problems.explain: ω = 380 × 2π = 760π radians per minute, so v = rω = 8 × 760π cm per minute. Per second, ÷ 60; in meters, ÷ 100: 6080π ÷ 60 ÷ 100 ≈ 3.1835, which is 3.2 to 1 decimal place. (Leaving out the 2π counts turns, not distance.) So 3.2 meters per second.

problems.explain: Each turn rolls one circumference, π × 75 cm. Per hour: π × 75 × 390 × 60 cm, and a kilometer is 100,000 cm: ≈ 55.135, which is 55.1 to 1 decimal place. (The wheel's diameter, not its radius, goes with π here.) So 55.1 kilometers per hour.
